- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates prices; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply a 15–25% downward correction to post-spike values.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed; if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average, adjust toward historical mean.
- Forecasts with high variance (e.g., >3.0 in 30d window) correlate with sentiment volatility; dampen extreme outliers, especially if sentiment history shows no clear trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates; apply upward bias to early 30d values, especially day 1–5.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >1.5x recent 7-day average), model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, especially if sentiment is rising.
